newsitem.title: USA: Jostens sees some plant consolidations.
newsitem.headline: Jostens sees some plant consolidations.

text.p: Jostens Inc said Tuesday it will likely consolidate some plants over the next two years.
It now has 16 plants in the United States and two in Canada.
Jostens, which provides products and services including yearbooks, class rings, and achievement awards, said it is focused on the upcoming school graduation season.

"The development of our go-to-market strategy for the college market is nearly completed, and we continue to make progress on our manufacturing analysis, as we evaluate our capacity requirements and determine our facilities configuration for the future," Robert Buhrmaster, president, said in a statement.
"It remains likely that we will have some plant consolidations over the next two years," he added.

Jostens reported earnings for the quarter ended December 28 of $0.11 a share versus $0.31 a year ago. Results are part of a stub year ended December 1996 as the company changes from a July-June fiscal year to a January-December year.
Jostens said a new inventory cost accounting system cut profits for the December quarter by shifting about $0.11 a share to the June 1997 quarter.
The quarter also included an increase of $6.0 million or $0.09 a share in reserves to cover continued environmental investigation and clean-up programs.
The company has programs underway at three sites.
